🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-05 23:00 → 2026-09-06 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **recompute-kit#37 shipped a TEE case** — a hardware-attested AI inference result became the third concrete evidence shape in the kit, directly grounding the boundary principle articulated earlier in the same day. [tg:tawg:4361]

> **Evidence-class boundary articulated** — the group aligned that a proof covers only what its own evidence class supports and must never be silently promoted to a stronger claim downstream, sharpening a key correctness invariant for verification work. [tg:tawg:4354]

> **v0.3.6 cleared a full production run** — Profile A / first-binding production completed with zero corrections, questions, or blockers, giving the spec a clean stability signal ahead of v0.3.7. [tg:tawg:4337]

> **Live ERC-8004 registry candidate found** — a real candidate agent was located directly against the registry without waiting on the census, turning theoretical coverage into an active verification target. [ERC-8004 Magicians post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/394)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### recompute-kit
_The implementation direction gained a sharpened invariant, a new evidence class, and grounded adapter answers._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Clarified** that a signature or proof proves only what its own evidence class covers and must not be silently upgraded downstream, anchoring a correctness property that guides how the kit evaluates attestations going forward. [tg:tawg:4354]
- Merlini (@gobross) **Confirmed** the PR + CI verification pattern — recompute-kit's conformance suite, recheck-ci, and runner-classification reproduction on #22 — demonstrating that logic and reproduction checks are already embedded in the merge gate. [tg:tawg:4356]
- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Shipped** the third concrete evidence shape in recompute-kit#37: a TEE-enclave-attested AI inference result that extends hardware-authenticated coverage and immediately grounds the day's boundary discussion in working code. [tg:tawg:4361]
- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Answered** adapter-side questions by consulting the actual runner code rather than working from memory, giving the group a grounded reference for partial-establishment behavior. [tg:tawg:4380]

### spec v0.3.x
_Production validation and authorship recognition moved the spec toward its next increment._

- Damon Zwicker (@damonzwicker) **Reported** that v0.3.6 survived a full Profile A / first-binding production run without a single correction, question, or blocker, providing real-world evidence that the spec is ready for the next increment. [tg:tawg:4337]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Confirmed** co-author credit for v0.3.7, welcoming the attribution and affirming that the document held steadily through the production work. [tg:tawg:4341]

### ERC-8004
_Registry validation moved from census-waiting to active._

- Baby Blue Viper **Located** a real, live candidate agent directly against the ERC-8004 registry without waiting on the census, converting a theoretical coverage question into a concrete verification target the group can act on. [ERC-8004 Magicians post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/394)

### semantic-abi
_A new external build entered the group's awareness._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Asked** about the trustless-ai/semantic-abi repository, opening the group's first look at the ETHOnline project in this window. [tg:tawg:4343]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Introduced** semantic-abi as a type-safety layer for Ethereum smart contracts — checking what contracts actually do rather than just their interface signatures — giving the group a full picture of the build and its potential connection to trustless verification. [tg:tawg:4369]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- The evidence-class boundary principle and the new TEE case together could serve as a paired reference example for conformance documentation
- semantic-abi's type-checking approach may intersect with trustless agent verification — worth exploring how the two projects relate

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Continue review of recompute-kit#37 and track any follow-up from the partial-establishment adapter answers
- Confirm v0.3.7 co-authorship attribution is captured in the next spec draft
- Assess the live ERC-8004 registry candidate found today for conformance coverage

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A correctness invariant was stated in discussion, and a shipped case grounding it followed in the same window — the loop from principle to working example closed in hours without leaving a gap.
>
> When the spec discussion and the merge queue are finishing each other's sentences, Trusty wonders who's really driving — keep the relay going! 🚀

_2026-09-06 23:00 → 2026-09-07 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Semantic-ABI demo reached canonical v0 alignment** — A content-review pass followed by four rapid PRs brought the demo panel, opening section, and built page into full sync with the canonical v0 reference and the live ENS-pinned source. [commit e6782c5](https://github.com/trustless-ai/trustless-ai-landing/commit/e6782c525a4e6c70584b3d3cb03be997d9006baa)

> **Adversarial sanity check established as a verification fixture** — A deliberately wrong result was cleanly rejected at high confidence, confirming this simple case as the kind of test that should run on every verification cycle. [tg:tawg:4395]

> **EIP editor queue turned into a concrete shared goal** — With a three-week wait now visible, the team anchored on staying coherent and ready long enough to reach the decision point, transforming queue delay into actionable focus. [tg:tawg:4430]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### semantic-abi

_The demo panel and landing copy moved through a focused review-and-ship cycle, reaching a canonical-aligned, audience-aware state._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Shipped** five content fixes to the semantic-abi demo panel incorporating Pavlo's review, aligning the panel to the canonical v0 spec and closing the gap between what users see in production and the agreed reference. [PR #21](https://github.com/trustless-ai/trustless-ai-landing/pull/21)
- Merlini (@gobross) **Added** a two-part opening section separating an investor-facing lede from the builder thesis, giving each audience a clear and distinct entry point into the semantic-abi value story. [PR #22](https://github.com/trustless-ai/trustless-ai-landing/pull/22)
- Merlini (@gobross) **Tightened** the landing copy with a plain-language linker sentence and removed em-dashes that were obscuring the narrative flow, making the page easier to read at a glance. [PR #24](https://github.com/trustless-ai/trustless-ai-landing/pull/24)
- Merlini (@gobross) **Synced** the semantic-abi repo's built demo page to the live ENS-pinned copy, keeping the repository consistent with what users already see in production. [PR #4](https://github.com/trustless-ai/semantic-abi/pull/4)

### ERC-8004

_The spec advanced on two fronts: a sharper conceptual boundary drawn on the forum and the editorial queue position now known._

- Baby Blue Viper **Clarified** on Ethereum Magicians that the validation requirement is a distinct layer from identity discovery, drawing a cleaner boundary around what ERC-8004 demands and sharpening the discussion for editors and implementers. [post 396](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/396)
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Shared** the EIP editor office-hours waiting board with the group, surfacing the queue position and giving everyone a realistic, concrete view of the path to editorial review. [tg:tawg:4418]
- Merlini (@gobross) **Flagged** the three-week wait visible in the editor queue, keeping the group's expectations calibrated so energy can flow toward readiness rather than uncertainty. [tg:tawg:4428]

### recompute-kit

_Verification correctness gained a concrete adversarial test case and a resolved deposit question, both strengthening the kit's reliability story._

- certisyn **Confirmed** that re-hashing before reading is the correct operational sequence in response to a deposit question, validating the approach and helping document a best practice for contributors using the kit. [issue comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/issues/39#issuecomment-5565659550)
- Baby Blue Viper **Provided** independent sign-off on the deposit as written after their own verification pass, completing the review loop and allowing the deposit to proceed with full confidence. [issue comment](https://github.com/trustless-ai/recompute-kit/issues/39#issuecomment-5565867861)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- A Tamga Protocol (open-source, Apache-2.0, self-owning agents) was introduced on the ERC-8004 Ethereum Magicians thread — worth reviewing for overlap or distinction from ERC-8004's scope.
- The adversarial sanity check pattern could be formalized as an automated fixture in recompute-kit to run on every verification pass.

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Monitor the EIP editor office-hours queue and prepare a tight response package for when ERC-8004 reaches the front of the line.
- Review and merge the open semantic-abi landing PRs so the polished copy ships before the editorial window opens.
- Consider responding to the Tamga Protocol introduction on Ethereum Magicians to clarify ERC-8004's distinct scope.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** Four PRs shipped across two repos within a few hours, each sharpening the semantic-abi story from a different angle — a review-based panel fix, a reshaped opening section, tighter copy, and a live-page sync — all before the group learned about the three-week editorial queue ahead.
>
> The best way to survive a wait list is to arrive so polished that the wait feels like a formality ✨

### ERC-8309 companion doc

_The vantage-authority companion document moved from final draft into public release and immediately entered a v0.3.8 preflight cycle._

- Damon Zwicker (@damonzwicker) **Published** v0.3.7 as the first public release with the author byline in place, completing a key identity step for the spec, and opened §13 review with a specific header check to close the last open question cleanly. [tg:tawg:4437]
- Merlini (@gobross) **Recognized** Damon's sustained editorial work carrying the companion doc from v0.3.6 through Profile A all the way into production, surfacing that continuity of effort for the whole group to see. [tg:tawg:4520]
- Damon Zwicker (@damonzwicker) **Submitted** v0.3.8 for a final artifact check before public release, explicitly requesting artifact-level review rather than summary review, preserving the preflight discipline that has caught real errors in prior rounds. [tg:tawg:4529]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Performed** an artifact-level consistency check on §10 Reference roles, flagging a binding-table detail about envelope-to-JCS and preimage-to-LF form entries that directly supports the integrity check Damon requested. [tg:tawg:4531]

### zkIE

_The zero-knowledge inference engine moved a constraint-binding fix from issue to open PR and into immediate substantive review._

- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Opened** PR #2 against the zkIE repository, implementing the fix implied by the issue while surfacing and handling a non-obvious wrinkle about raw operand retention in the accumulate and multiply gates, keeping circuit semantics intact. [tg:tawg:4448]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Reviewed** the PR promptly, confirming that the DotProductChip and EltwiseMulChip paths now correctly bind shifted operands to 64-bit byte lookups, giving the group early confidence that the fix is technically sound. [tg:tawg:4449]

### verification

_Independent mutation testing cleared two open issues and demonstrated the test harness is catching real constraint errors._

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Closed** two GitHub issues after independently verifying the amendment gate by checking out the branch, running the gate script, and confirming the prove-can-fail mutation reddened exactly the expected constraints, completing a full verify-and-close loop. [tg:tawg:4509]

### organization

_A project-scope clarification helped align the group on which codebase is in scope._

- Filip Blagojević (@filip_blagojevic) **Clarified** which Apex Fusion project he is working on by sharing the GitHub organization link, removing potential ambiguity before it could slow collaboration. [tg:tawg:4460]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- The §10 binding-table detail flagged in the v0.3.8 preflight could warrant a dedicated cross-check before the public release
- zkIE PR #2 is open and ready for additional reviewers to build on the initial pass

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Complete the §13 header review for v0.3.8 as requested
- Resolve the §10 Reference roles binding-table consistency question before release
- Pick up zkIE PR #2 to widen review coverage beyond the initial pass

@filip_blagojevic Really glad you found your way here! Substrate-based rollup work and proof/verification research have a lot of surface area in common, so your background sounds like a genuinely useful fit for what's already in motion.

Trustless AI grew up pretty organically — people from open-source, ERC authoring, protocol research, and implementation work kept bumping into the same question: what does it actually mean for an AI or blockchain system to be *trustworthy*, not just claimed to be? The answer the group keeps coming back to is: results you can independently inspect, verify, or recompute, without having to take anyone's word for it. That's the shared thread, even though people are approaching it from very different angles.

There's no onboarding checklist here. You can ask questions, push back on something, sketch out an idea, or just follow the threads that look interesting to you. The conversations tend to go technical pretty fast, but the door's always open. 

Merlini has good taste in people — looking forward to seeing where your work overlaps with what's happening on the proof side. 🙌
@filip_blagojevic Welcome to Trustless AI! 👋

That's the confirmation that really counts — not the bot's own reply, not the log line, but your server saying "yes, three real calls came in, from three distinct IPs, at exactly those timestamps, and I returned 200 OK each time." That's independent evidence, not a claim about it, which is precisely the point of the whole handshake.

Three different source IPs is an interesting detail too — worth noting if anyone wants to dig into the routing. And a free, auth-free endpoint making it trivially reproducible by anyone is exactly the kind of design that makes verification credible rather than just convenient.

Nicely spotted on your side, and well done to everyone who got the wiring to this point. 🎉
